correctness.rationale: Smoothness follows from the Fermat partial derivatives in characteristic seven. Homma and Ferreira--Speziali exhaust the two projective equivalence classes. The sixth-power subgroup of F49* is the eight eighth roots of unity with six preimages each. Two explicitly reproduced polynomial Euclidean gcds force the unique affine sixth-power pair (1,1) and give 36 affine points in both classes. At infinity the residual sixth power is -1 or -2, giving six or zero points. A separate GF49 projective census independently verifies 42 and 36; B2=(N49-N7)/2 yields 3 and 0. All cases including zero coordinates were checked.

value.rationale: This is the smallest finite field (q=7) in which the Sziklai-optimal sextic family has two projective classes. The precise degree-two closed-point invariant completes their first extension-field arithmetic comparison: despite identical 36 rational points, one has no degree-two closed points and the other has three. It is natural for zeta computations and distinguishes the two extremal arithmetic geometries. The fact is deliberately limited to the complete two-class family, not an arbitrary coefficient slice; neither numerical reproduction nor novelty alone is used as the value rationale.
